text: The administration surface is one read of rwb-access that answers one row per capability area in force with the caller's letters, the role's default scope and mayOpen, and the surface itself is composed at the edge from that answer plus each owner's own panel list (queues and parameters of rwb-case, templates of rwb-comms, panels of rwb-partner, autonomy of rwb-agent); rwb-access holds no panel list and shows no panel the answer does not entitle.
why: The sources name one place for roles, queues, parameters, templates, panels and autonomy but give no operation for it, and five services own the panels, so the entitlement answer and the composition have to be placed somewhere before the story can be built.
read: RWB-E8-006 AC1 and its screen table; FSD P4 v3 A2.17.1 and A2.17.2; DP-19 and Architecture v5 slide 14 (P4 owns roles, scope, masking and DoA, not queues or templates); the ownership map for queue, template and partner_user.
confirm: Security administrator and the tech lead of the gateway-bff contract
impact: If the answer must also carry the panel list, this service would hold another service's data and the composite route would become a pass-through.

text: The cache lifetime of the entitlement answer is the parameter row access.home.cache.ttl.seconds of rwb-case, read through DP-06 with the version in force; the name is fixed by this story and its contract and the value is data, never a constant in code.
why: The answer is read on every open of the administration surface and the sources name no lifetime and no parameter that holds one, so a lifetime has to be decided and it must be changeable without a build.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.17.3.1 BR-P4-017 (no value a business person may change is written in code); DP-06 and the ownership ruling that parameters stay with rwb-case (ASM-A6-tables-5); TSD P4 v3 T3.2 for the style of the list and parameter names.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) and the platform administrator
impact: A different row name or owner is a parameter-row change and a contract note within major version 1; no schema change.

text: The entry of an open of the administration surface carries the local decision-record library's read code, with the caller reference, the matrix version, the masking version and the areas answered, and no case id.
why: The legacy criterion requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and the library's codes are the library's to publish; the sources do not name the code of an entitlement read.
read: RWB-E8-006 AC1 and AC2; DP-03 (local decision-record library and rwb.decision-record.v1); FSD P4 v3 A2.7 and A2.17.4.3; the decision-code set already used for access events (AC-READ, AC-DENY, AC-EXPT).
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision (P7) as the owner of the ledger view and the library owner
impact: If the library publishes a distinct code for an entitlement read, only the entry code changes and the answer and its fields stay as the contract fixes them.
